subject: Urgent: Lumos integration - support SLA coordination and on-call alignment
messages:
From: Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 17:14:00 -0800
Subject: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads-up — since ~15:30 PST today Lumos's customers in the analytics tier have started seeing intermittent 504s for calls that proxy through Redwood's hosted inference for our shared integration. Error rates spiked to ~6% for 30m and are currently fluctuating. Our ops team collected request traces and a short excerpt is attached (lumos_error_log_excerpt.txt).

This is affecting three paying customers (two in NA, one in EU). We need to confirm:
- Is Redwood treating this as an actionable SLA incident for partner integrations?
- Who is the on-call for Redwood that we should escalate to if errors persist after a fix?

We attempted a rollback to the previous model variant on our side but the errors persisted, which suggests an upstream routing/capacity issue. Can you confirm receipt and propose next steps?

Thanks,
Kate Robinson
Head of Integrations | Lumos Analytics

Attachment: lumos_error_log_excerpt.txt
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 17:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Hi Kate — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. I’m escalating to on-call and ops immediately. Short answers up front: yes, we treat partner-facing production outages as SLA incidents under our Partner SLA addendum; and Sean (cc'd) is the on-call for Redwood infra this week.

Planned immediate steps:
1) Sean will examine routing/queue saturation and check for degraded model variants.
2) Dylan will validate whether our edge routing to the region where the EU customer lives had a transient outage.
3) If a mitigation requires capacity burst, we can open a Dedicated burst lane for Lumos while we triage.

Can you confirm the three impacted customer names and the approximate business impact (queries/min, revenue tier) so we can prioritize? Also, please keep the traces coming if you see additional 5xx patterns.

I’ll coordinate an incident bridge if required.

— Marissa
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 18:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Kate, Marissa — I pulled the traces and saw clear signs of transient queue spikes in the us-west-2 pool between 15:10-15:50 PST. Some requests hit queue depth limits and were rejected, resulting in 504s. I kicked an autoscale policy to add two nodes and also flushed a stuck KV-cache that appeared to be associated with the latest model variant we rolled.

Immediate asks from Lumos:
- Can Lumos temporarily reduce batch sizes for high-priority customers (we noticed batch size 64->32 would reduce tail latency)?
- Can you confirm whether any client-side retries were aggressively replaying requests?

I’ve opened SUP-9421 and started a short-term mitigation (capacity burst). Monitoring now. If error rate drops below 0.5% for 20m I’ll call it mitigated and propose a follow-up root cause analysis.

Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Engineer (On-call) | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 18:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Thanks Sean — appreciate the swift action. Quick answers:
- Lumos confirmed the three impacted customers: AlphaGeo (enterprise), BrightMetrics (midmarket), and QuantileInsights (pilot). AlphaGeo is the highest priority (VIP).
- We are not intentionally replaying requests; there may be an SDK retry loop in an older client version. We’ll check and cut a canary with retries disabled.

Can Redwood confirm whether the temporary burst will be billed under our partner burst credit or billed to our account directly? Also, please share the bridge link if you spin one up.

Ben 
Systems Engineer | Lumos Analytics
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>, Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Ben — Redwood will apply partner emergency burst credits for today’s mitigation (per our partner escalation playbook) while we investigate cost attribution. I’ve created a joint runbook draft (joint-runbook-v1.pdf) — it includes on-call handoffs, escalation matrix, and a set of temporary mitigations (batch size, retry settings, model pinning).

I propose a coordination call tomorrow at 10:00 PST to align on: post-mitigation testing, SDK release to disable retries, and scheduled RCA. Can you confirm? We’ll send a calendar invite with bridge + Zoom and share the Atlassian ticket link.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Kate Robinson <kate@lumosanalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@lumosanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts hitting Lumos customers - need SLA pathing

Marissa/Team — Confirmed for 10:00 PST tomorrow (2026-02-14). We’ll cut the SDK canary (retries disabled) against AlphaGeo first and run load tests for 45 minutes. Thanks for the burst credit — that’s helpful to keep AlphaGeo online while you investigate.

Two small asks before the call:
1) Please add an explicit contact for after-hours escalations (phone or pager) into the runbook.
2) Can Redwood provide an initial hypothesis summary in the call so we can prepare questions?

See you on the bridge — Kate

Attachment: joint-runbook-v1.pdf
